oi.heading: Income from Operations
oi.text:
Income from operations in our Hardware and Protective Solutions segment decreased $13.0 million due to the changes in net sales, cost of sales, SG&A expenses, and other income described above in addition to an increase in depreciation expense of $0.8 million due to capital spend on merchandising racks and amortization of $0.8 million due to the Kanebridge acquisition.

Income from operations in our Robotics and Digital Solutions segment increased $1.8 million. The $1.8 million increase is primarily due to the changes in net sales, cost of sales, and SG&A expenses described above, partially offset by an increase in depreciation expense of $1.5 million due to capital spend on key duplication kiosks and machines. Additionally, we saw an increase of $0.2 million in other income driven by the changes in revaluation of the contingent consideration described above.

Canada's income from operations increased by $3.2 million primarily due to the changes in net sales, cost of sales and SG&A expenses described above partially offset by the change in exchange rate gains of $0.2 million in the thirteen weeks ended September 26, 2026.

Interest expense, net, decreased $0.4 million in the thirteen weeks ended September 26, 2026.

opex.heading: Other Operating Expenses
opex.text:
Depreciation expense increased $2.2 million due to capital spend on merchandising racks and key duplication kiosks.

Amortization expense in the thirteen weeks ended September 26, 2026 increased $0.4 million primarily due to the additional amortization of intangible assets related to the Kanebridge acquisition.

In the thirteen weeks ended September 26, 2026, other income (expense) increased by $1.4 million consisting primarily of a $0.8 million gain in rebate income along with a $0.5 million gain on the acquisition of Campbell Chain and Fittings (see Note 4 - Acquisitions of the Notes to Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information) and a $0.1 million gain on the revaluation of the contingent consideration associated with the acquisition of Resharp and Instafob (see Note 15 - Fair Value Measurements of the Notes to Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information).

In the thirteen weeks ended September 27, 2025, other income (expense) consisted primarily of exchange rate losses of $0.2 million and a $0.1 million loss on the revaluation of the contingent consideration associated with the acquisition of Resharp and Instafob. In addition, we recorded income related to certain rebates received of $0.3 million.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
For the thirteen weeks ended September 26, 2026 and thirteen weeks ended September 27, 2025, the effective income tax rate was 37.4% and 25.7%, respectively. The Company recorded an income tax provision for the thirteen weeks ended September 26, 2026 of $3.8 million on pre-tax income of $10.0 million, and an income tax provision for the thirteen weeks ended September 27, 2025 of $8.0 million based on a pre-tax income of $31.2 million.

The Company applies an estimated annual effective tax rate (“AETR”) to year-to-date ordinary income in each interim period. In 2026, the effective tax rate differed from the U.S. federal statutory rate mainly due to non-deductible expenses and state and foreign income taxes, partially offset by the non-taxable gain on the acquisition of Campbell Chain and Fittings. The increase in the effective tax rate compared to the prior year period was primarily due to lower forecasted annual pre-tax income, which increased the relative impact of non-deductible expenses and state and foreign income taxes on the AETR.

In 2025, the effective tax rate differed from the U.S. federal statutory tax rate mainly due to state and foreign income taxes and non-deductible expenses.

net.text: • Net income for the thirteen weeks ended September 26, 2026 was $6.3 million, or $0.03 per diluted share, compared to net income of $23.2 million, or $0.12 per diluted share for the thirteen weeks ended September 27, 2025.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities for the thirty-nine weeks ended September 26, 2026 was favorably impacted by a reduction in inventory due to a focus on inventory management in order to balance supply chain in relationship with the recently enacted tariffs. Additionally, net cash used for operating activities was unfavorably impacted by increases in accounts receivable due to the seasonality of our business along with pricing actions taken with our customers in response to the cost increases. Finally, net cash provided by operating activities was unfavorably impacted by a decrease in accrued incentive compensation related to the payout of 2025 incentive compensation.

da.text:
The following table summarizes cost of sales by segment:

Hardware and Protective Solutions' cost of sales as a percentage of net sales increased primarily due to increased tariff costs and product costs.

Robotics and Digital Solutions' cost of sales as a percentage of net sales decreased due to our price increases and sales mix.

Canada's cost of sales as a percentage of net sales decreased primarily due to decreased product and shipping costs.

wc.text: Our working capital position, which we define as current assets minus current liabilities, of $432.3 million as of September 26, 2026 represents an increase of $43.4 million from the December 27, 2025 level of $388.9 million. $43.3 million of the increase is related the acquisition of Kanebridge Corporation that occurred in August 2026, $6.6 million of the increase is related to the Campbell Chain and Fittings acquisition that incurred in April 2026 and $4.6 million of the increase is related to the Delaney Hardware acquisition that occurred in April 2026. The increase in working capital is offset by seasonality of the business and tariff costs. We expect to generate sufficient operating cash flows to meet our short-term liquidity needs, and we expect to maintain access to the capital markets, although there can be no assurance of our ability to do so. However, disruption and volatility in the global capital markets and economic uncertainties driven by increases in tariffs could impact our capital resources and liquidity in the future. We do expect the current tariff environment to increase our costs of products we import, which will increase our working capital position and unfavorably impact our future cash flows (see Recent Developments - Tariff Environment of Item 2 - Management’s Discussion and Analysis).

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures:
capex.text: Cash of $51.4 million and $55.3 million was used in the thirty-nine weeks ended September 26, 2026 and thirty-nine weeks ended September 27, 2025, respectively, to invest in new key duplicating kiosks and merchandising racks.

net sales.heading: Net Sales by Segment
net sales.text:
We evaluate our net sales growth by measuring changes from new business wins (e.g. new customers, new product lines, or new categories at existing customers), mergers and acquisitions, and core performance of the existing business. We define core performance as the impact of the following factors on our existing base of business: market volume growth, change in customer footprint, product category management, price increases

and/or decreases, and the impact of foreign currency exchange. During the quarter, our business was impacted by macroeconomic influences like economic uncertainty and concerns over housing affordability resulting from the combined pressure of high home prices and elevated interest rates, both of which we believe impact existing home sales and repair and remodel spending on the home. During the third quarter of 2026, net sales increased by $32.5 million or 7.7%, and drivers of the increase are detailed below.

Our Hardware and Protective Solutions' segment increased by $17.8 million, or 5.4%. Primarily driving the increase was a 6.1% or $20.0 million increase in net sales related to the Delaney, Campbell, and Kanebridge acquisitions along with a 1.7% increase in new business wins. Offsetting the increase in sales was a decrease of 2.3% in core performance.

intro.text: Founded in 1964 and headquartered in Cincinnati, Hillman is a leading provider of hardware and related products serving retail, pro distribution, and industrial customers. Over the last 60-plus years, Hillman has built a legacy of service and growth by forming strategic partnerships with North America’s leading home improvement, hardware, and farm and fleet retailers. Hillman differentiates itself from the competition with its dedicated field sales team of 1,200+ associates, direct-to-store distribution capabilities, and world class global sourcing and supply chain expertise.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: We sell our products to a large volume of customers, the top two of which accounted for approximately $674.3 million, or approximately 43% of our total revenues in 2025.

For the year ended December 27, 2025, Home Depot was the single largest customer, representing approximately $349.9 million or 22.5% of our total revenues and Lowe's was the second largest customer at approximately $324.4 million or 20.9% of our total revenues.
No other customer accounted for more than 10% of total revenues in 2025.
For the year ended December 27, 2025, the largest two customers, Lowe's and Home Depot, accounted for 43.4 % of total revenues and 28.7 % of the year-end accounts receivable balance.
For the year ended December 28, 2024, the largest two customers accounted for 40.9 % of total revenues and 32.6 % of the year end accounts receivable balance.
Except as described in the paragraphs above, no other customer accounted for more than 10% of the Company's accounts receivables in 2025 or 2024.
You should not rely on these forward-looking statements as predictions of future events.

We currently manage a worldwide supply chain comprised of a large number of vendors, the largest of which accounted for approximately 7.6% of the Company's annual purchases and the top five of which accounted for approximately 17.2% of our annual purchases.
In addition, we are the primary supplier of Metal Shapes to many wholesalers throughout the country.

The Company does not believe a sales concentration exists in these scenarios, as the independently owned hardware stores can continue to make purchases from the Company via a direct bill arrangement or via another purchasing cooperative.
The success of our efforts to grow our business depends on the contributions and abilities of key executives, our sales force, and other personnel.

Our long-term success in the current competitive environment depends on our ability to develop and commercialize a continuing stream of innovative new products which create and maintain consumer demand.
We import a majority of our products and rely on foreign sources, primarily China and Taiwan, to meet our supply demands at prices that support our current operating margins.

However, it is not always possible to replace a vendor on short notice without disruption in our operations, which may require more costly expedited transportation expense and replacement of a major vendor is often at higher prices.
Because our business is working capital intensive, we rely on our ability to manage our product purchasing and customer credit policies.
Successful sales and marketing efforts depend on our ability to recruit and retain qualified employees.

The success of our efforts to grow our business depends on the contributions and abilities of key executives, our sales force, and other personnel, including the ability of our sales force to achieve adequate customer coverage.

We depend on our information systems, and those of our third party vendors and business partners, to process orders, to manage inventory and accounts receivable collections, to purchase, sell, and ship products efficiently and on a timely basis, to maintain cost-effective operations, and to provide superior service to our customers.
We rely on various information systems and technology to manage our business.

We rely on available borrowings under the Asset-Based Revolving credit facility (“ABL Revolver”) for cash to operate our business, and the availability of credit under the ABL Revolver may be subject to significant fluctuation.
A 5% difference in actual excess and obsolete inventory reserved for at December 27, 2025 would have affected net earnings by approximately $1.6 million in fiscal 2025.
